cards.text: Honeybees are insects that live in large hives.
They make sweet honey from flower nectar.
Worker bees collect pollen on their back legs.
A queen bee lays all the eggs.
Honeybees communicate by doing a waggle dance.
Butterflies taste their food with their feet.
Ants build tunnels under the dirt.
These facts show how honeybees live and work.
Frogs are amphibians that can live on land.
They catch flying bugs with long, sticky tongues.
Most frogs lay their eggs in water.
Baby frogs hatch out as swimming tadpoles.
Frogs can absorb water through their skin.
Turtles carry hard shells on their backs.
Toads have dry, bumpy skin.
Now you know all about frogs.
The moon is a rocky sphere orbiting Earth.
Craters cover the dusty surface of the moon.
Footprints stay on the moon for many years.
The moon reflects bright light from the sun.
Astronauts walked on the moon in spacesuits.
Mars has red dust covering its ground.
Stars are giant balls of burning gas.
As you can see, the moon is special.
